items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: So that was my first association listening to him, and then we became close friends, and next worked together in New York.

ctx.x: And that's -- primarily to get to the point, that's how I met Bobby Hackett. And it wasn't long before the word got out all over the country about this little cornet player down in Boston that sounded so much like Bix, and that's before Bix's big image across the country was on a few elite privileged people who knew about Bix, and his playing and had the records.

So Brad Gowans talked to Bobby about this, and it wasn't long before the whole country was hearing about this wonderful clarinet player, as I said, that sounded like Bix. So that was my first association listening to him, and then we became close friends, and next worked together in New York. Of course, there's a span of time there. This was, as I said, in 1934-5, and Bobby came to New York and went into the original Nick's in New York on 7th Avenue and 11th Street.

And he played there for four or five years, and we did several jazz concerts here and there, but my first long association with Bobby was when he took me into Nick's which we talked about before -- he took me in there in late '39, and our association musically went on from there.
